decisive_items: Each episode featured subjective perioral swelling, hypotension within her baseline range, and stridor that resolved without objective edema
Direct laryngoscopy during one episode showed no airway edema or paradoxical vocal cord motion
Serial serum tryptase levels during acute events remained normal
response.rationale: Recurrent episodes of presumed anaphylaxis with only subjective swelling, no objective edema, normal tryptase, and normal laryngoscopy indicate feigned/factitious symptoms rather than organic anaphylaxis or unconscious somatoform symptoms; psychiatric history and eating-disorder setting support a self-imposed factitious disorder.

rejected.why: No evidence a caregiver is fabricating or inducing illness; symptoms are self-reported by the patient.
Normal serial tryptase and equivocal bone marrow biopsy do not support mastocytosis; no objective mediator release.
Normal tryptase and absence of objective findings contradict true or induced anaphylaxis.
Less specific; symptoms appear deliberately feigned rather than unconsciously somatoform, and repeated PICU admissions without objective findings favor factitious disorder.
Unremarkable mast cell mediator workup and normal tryptase contradict inducible mast cell activation syndrome.
Normal hereditary angioedema testing and no objective edema contradict hereditary angioedema.
